prompt: `az storage blob list --delimiter /` answers `exports/` for a container that holds three blobs. What is `exports/`?
hint: Ask whether anything was ever created under that name.

choices.text: A directory object Blob Storage made when the first blob was uploaded
choices.why: No such object exists; `az storage blob show` on the prefix answered `BlobNotFound`.

choices.text: A zero-byte blob whose name ends in a slash
choices.why: Nothing in this lesson wrote one, and the prefix appeared anyway.

choices.text: A group of names, computed for this listing
choices.why: Right. The service grouped every name at its first slash; delete the blobs and the group is gone.

choices.text: A second container nested inside `orders-raw`
choices.why: Containers do not nest; there is one level of them per account.

prompt: A program lists `--prefix exports/2026/` and gets nothing, although the files are there. Their names start with `Exports/2026/`. Why?
hint: How are two names compared?

choices.text: Blob names are case-sensitive, so the two prefixes differ
choices.why: Right. `EXPORTS/...` answered `exists: false` in the lesson for the same reason.

choices.text: A prefix only works together with `--delimiter`
choices.why: A prefix filters on its own; the delimiter only groups what is left.

choices.text: The listing needs a trailing `*` to match
choices.why: A prefix is matched literally from the start of the name, with no wildcards.

choices.text: Listings by prefix are cached for a few minutes after an upload
choices.why: There is no such cache; a listing reads the current names.

prompt: Quitanda wants to read one month of exports without listing the names of every other month. Which naming does that?
hint: A listing walks names in order and filters on the start of the name.

choices.text: `orders-2026-10-27.csv` at the root, then filter in the program
choices.why: Filtering in the program means listing every name first.

choices.text: `exports/c-17/orders-2026-10-27.csv`, grouped by customer
choices.why: The month is now after the customer, so one month is spread under every customer's prefix.

choices.text: Any of them, with the month stored in each blob's metadata
choices.why: Metadata cannot be searched; finding it means reading every blob's metadata.

choices.text: `exports/2026/10/orders-2026-10-27.csv`
choices.why: Right. `--prefix exports/2026/10/` asks the service for that month alone.

prompt: Match each piece of data to the blob type it belongs in.
hint: Ask how each one is written: whole, at the end, or anywhere.

pairs.left: The nightly orders export, written once
The checkout service's log, a line at a time
A Parquet file for the analysts

prompt: Three blocks have been staged for a new blob and nothing has been committed. What does a reader get?
hint: `blocks.py` asked `exists()` at that moment.

choices.text: The three blocks, in the order they were staged
choices.why: Staged blocks are invisible to readers until a commit names them.

choices.text: Nothing: the blob does not exist yet
choices.why: Right. `exists before the commit: False`.

choices.text: The first block only, until the others are confirmed
choices.why: There is no partial read of staged blocks.

choices.text: An error saying the blob is locked by an upload
choices.why: Staging takes no lock; the blob is simply absent.

prompt: The nightly upload of a 2 GB export crashes after half of its blocks. What do the analysts read the next morning under that name?
hint: Which request makes a block blob change?

choices.text: Half of the new file, followed by the end of the old one
choices.why: Blocks are never mixed into a readable blob without a commit.

choices.text: The previous complete version, or nothing if there was none
choices.why: Right. Without the commit the blob is unchanged; the staged blocks wait unseen.

choices.text: Half of the new file, which is why exports are checked by row count
choices.why: A row count is a fine check, but half a file is not what they would read.

choices.text: An empty blob of 2 GB filled with zeros
choices.why: That is how an unwritten page of a page blob reads, not a block blob.

prompt: A file of 646,670 bytes is uploaded with `max_single_put_size` and `max_block_size` both set to 256 KiB (262,144 bytes). How many blocks are committed?
hint: Full blocks, then one with the remainder.

prompt: A corrected order changes one line in the middle of a large export that was uploaded in blocks. What is the cheapest correct way to fix the blob?
hint: `blocks.py` did this in its last part.

choices.text: Append the corrected line at the end and let readers keep the last one
choices.why: A block blob does not take appends, and readers would see both lines.

choices.text: Upload the whole file again
choices.why: Correct, and the most expensive way: every block travels again.

choices.text: Write the corrected bytes at their offset
choices.why: Writing at an offset is what a page blob does; a block blob has no such operation.

choices.text: Stage the block holding that line again under its id, then commit the same list
choices.why: Right. Only that block travels; the commit swaps it in and keeps the rest.

prompt: The checkout log is an append blob. What does `az storage blob upload --overwrite` do to it?
hint: The lesson ran it and then asked for the blob's type.

choices.text: Replaces it with a new block blob holding the file
choices.why: Right. `BlockBlob`, 64 bytes, and the next append failed with `InvalidBlobType`.

choices.text: Refuses, because an append blob only accepts appends
choices.why: The type limits writes into the blob, not replacing it. The upload succeeded.

choices.text: Appends the file's bytes at the end of the log, after the six lines already there
choices.why: An upload is not an append; the six log lines were gone afterwards.

choices.text: Asks for confirmation before replacing a log
choices.why: `--overwrite` is the confirmation; nothing else is asked.

prompt: A page blob is made of pages of ___ bytes, and its size must be a multiple of that.
hint: 1,000 was refused and 1,024 was accepted.

prompt: `pages.py` printed `100 bytes refused before sending` with a Python message rather than an error code. Who refused?
hint: An error code comes back from a service.

choices.text: Azurite, which rejects any write under 512 bytes
choices.why: The request never reached Azurite; a service refusal carries a code.

choices.text: The operating system, because 100 bytes is below a disk sector
choices.why: No disk was touched; this is a network call that was never made.

choices.text: The Python library, which checked the alignment itself
choices.why: Right. It raised `ValueError` without sending anything.

choices.text: Docker, which limits the size of a request to a container
choices.why: Docker forwards the port and reads nothing.

prompt: Quitanda's auditors want the checkout log kept so that nobody, Quitanda's own engineers included, can rewrite it. Is making it an append blob enough?
hint: What did one upload with `--overwrite` do?

choices.text: Yes, because blocks already appended cannot be modified
choices.why: Not modified one by one, but the blob as a whole can be replaced or deleted.

choices.text: Yes, as long as only the logging program has the account key
choices.why: The requirement includes Quitanda's own engineers, who can obtain the key.

choices.text: No; it should be a page blob, since pages cannot be deleted
choices.why: A page blob is rewritable at any offset, the opposite of what is asked.

choices.text: No; it needs an immutability policy that refuses overwrite and delete
choices.why: Right. Lesson 5 covers those policies.

prompt: A program sets metadata `rows=2` and `source=shop`, then later calls metadata update with only `rows=3`. What does the blob carry afterwards?
hint: The lesson ran exactly this.

choices.text: `rows=3` and `source=shop`
choices.why: That would be a merge, and there is no merge operation.

choices.text: `rows=2`, `rows=3` and `source=shop`, kept as a history of values
choices.why: Metadata keeps no history; each name has one value.

choices.text: `rows=3` alone
choices.why: Right. The update replaces the whole set.

choices.text: An `InvalidMetadata` error, since `rows` already exists
choices.why: `InvalidMetadata` came from the hyphen in `row-count`, not from an existing name.

prompt: Which of these are true of a blob's ETag? Choose all that apply.
hint: Compare the ETag before and after the metadata update.

choices.text: It changes when only the metadata changes
choices.why: Yes; the lesson printed two different ETags around one metadata update.

choices.text: It is the MD5 of the content, in hexadecimal
choices.why: The MD5 is a separate property, `contentMd5`, in base64. The ETag is an opaque stamp.

choices.text: Given to `--if-match`, it makes a write conditional
choices.why: Yes; that is the only thing it is for.

choices.text: Two blobs with the same bytes have the same ETag
choices.why: It stamps a version of one blob and says nothing about content.

prompt: A query engine reads a Parquet file from Blob Storage and fails because the file reports `text/plain`. Which part of the blob is wrong?
hint: It is a header the uploader set, or let the tool guess.

choices.text: Its metadata, which should carry `format=parquet`
choices.why: Metadata is never interpreted by the service or by readers that do not know your names.

choices.text: Its content-type property, set or guessed at upload
choices.why: Right. The command line guessed `text/csv` from `.csv`; whoever uploaded this file let it be guessed wrong.

choices.text: Its blob type, which should be page rather than block for binary data such as Parquet
choices.why: Binary files are block blobs like any other file.

choices.text: Its tier, because hot blobs are served as text
choices.why: A tier changes price and availability, not how bytes are labelled.

prompt: `etag.py`'s second copy is refused. Which HTTP status comes back?
hint: A precondition failed.

choices.why: Right. Precondition failed, `ConditionNotMet`.
409 is a conflict, which `BlobAlreadyExists` uses.
403 is a refusal of permission, which is lesson 6.
The blob exists; it is the condition that failed.

prompt: A program's conditional write is refused with `ConditionNotMet`. What should it do?
hint: The refusal means somebody wrote since you read.

choices.text: Retry the same write until it succeeds
choices.why: It never will: the ETag it sends is stale, so every retry is refused the same way.

choices.text: Write again without the condition, since its data is the newest and the newest should win
choices.why: That is the silent overwrite the condition was there to prevent.

choices.text: Read the blob again and decide whether its write still makes sense
choices.why: Right. In `etag.py`, copy B would find the marker already at `2026-10-30` and stop.

choices.text: Acquire a lease and write with it
choices.why: A lease would let it write, and would overwrite the other copy's work just the same.

prompt: A job holds a 60-second lease on a manifest blob and crashes. What happens to other writers?
hint: A finite lease has to be renewed.

choices.text: They are refused with `LeaseIdMissing` until the lease runs out
choices.why: Right. Nobody renews it, so after its 60 seconds the blob is writable again.

choices.text: They can write at once, because the lease ends with the process
choices.why: The service cannot see the process die; it only sees the lease expire.

choices.text: They are refused for good, until somebody deletes the blob
choices.why: That would be an infinite lease; this one lasts 60 seconds.

choices.text: They are refused with 412 `ConditionNotMet`
choices.why: That is the ETag refusal; a missing lease id has its own code.

prompt: Put the steps of a safe update to a shared marker blob in order.
hint: Read, decide, write with a condition, handle the refusal.
items: Read the marker and keep its ETag
Decide the new value from what was read
Write with `If-Match` set to the kept ETag
On a 412, read again and start over

prompt: Which of these writes can a block blob accept?
hint: Think of what `blocks.py` did, and what failed on the log.

choices.text: Writing 512 bytes at offset 1024
choices.why: That is a page blob's write.

choices.text: Appending a block at the end
choices.why: Refused with `InvalidBlobType`, as the logger found.

choices.text: Changing its type to append
choices.why: The type is fixed when the blob is created.

choices.text: A commit of a new block list
choices.why: Right. That is the only way a block blob changes.

prompt: Without `--overwrite`, `az storage blob upload` refuses an existing blob with the error code ___.
hint: Three English words run together.
